html:
The imperial dynasty that ruled China from 960 to 1279. It was the richest, most urban and most inventive society of its time, though never the strongest militarily.

It was founded by Zhao Kuangyin, Emperor Taizu, a general who took the throne in 960 and ended the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period that followed the Tang. Wary of generals, the Song put civil officials, chosen through the imperial examination, firmly in charge.

Two halves:

  • Northern Song (960 to 1127), with its capital at Kaifeng. It paid the Liao to keep peace.
  • Southern Song (1127 to 1279). The Jurchen Jin took Kaifeng in 1127, and the court fled south to Lin'an, modern Hangzhou.

Even the smaller southern state was huge and rich. Fast-ripening Champa rice fed a growing population. The state issued paper money, the first government notes. Cities grew, and the scenes of Along the River at Qingming show their bustle. Woodblock printing spread books, and Bi Sheng invented movable type. Song writers set down the first gunpowder formulas, and Song ships steered by the magnetic compass. Shen Kuo wrote on science, and Zhu Xi shaped Neo-Confucianism, the official teaching for centuries after.

The Mongols destroyed the Jin in 1234 and then turned on the Song. The Song held out for decades. Kublai Khan took Hangzhou in 1276, and the last Song loyalists were crushed at sea at Yamen in 1279. China passed to the Yuan.
sum: The imperial dynasty that ruled China from 960 to 1279. It was the richest, most urban and most inventive society of its time, though never the strongest militarily.
